title: Config-drift sentinel: latency-vs-quality gating for batching+cache deltas
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: build an automated sentinel that estimates the latency-vs-quality frontier for small config deltas affecting batching and KV cache behavior and produces a single 'delta-risk' score to gate rollouts. Motivation: recent config rollouts (microbatch size, cache TTL, packing policy) caused regressions that only appeared on specific latency-sensitive slices and on long-context prompts. This ticket implements a reproducible eval harness and monitoring pipeline that ties per-request telemetry, reference prompt buckets, and synthetic adversarial prompts together to produce actionable signals for canary and auto-rollbacks.

Scope and approach:
- Define a compact but expressive config-delta matrix: microbatch sizes {1,2,4,8}, batch-shape policies {packed, permissive, strict}, prefix cache TTLs {0,30s,5m,1h}, cache-eviction modes {LRU, size-based}. Each candidate config is compared to a pinned baseline (runtime-1.20 default).
- Execution harness: replay ~10k representative requests sampled from production traces (with privacy-preserving sampling) + 1k synthetic hard prompts (long-context, truncated tokenization edge cases, structured-output tasks). Runs executed on identical infra to isolate software-level effects.
- Quality metrics: composite LQ score built from three signals: (1) embedding-similarity to golden responses (cosine similarity using eval-embed-v2), (2) structured-output schema pass-rate (for function-calling and JSON outputs), and (3) heuristic hallucination classifier pass/fail. We weight signals to prioritize functional correctness for structured tasks.
- Latency metrics: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, per-token latency, cold-start tail, and batching efficiency (tokens/sec per-GPU). Also capture distribution of microbatch occupancy and KV cache hit-rate per slice.
- Slicing: compute metrics per slice by prompt fingerprint: prompt-length buckets, domain bucket (conversation, code, instructions), customer-defined feature flags. Use fingerprint-based bucketing so future prompts map to existing slices.
- Delta-risk calculation: combine normalized quality delta and normalized latency delta into a single risk scalar. Quality regressions are amplified (weight 3x) relative to latency degradations for slices that are customer-visible. Risk thresholds: green < 0.05, amber 0.05-0.15, red > 0.15. Thresholds are configurable per-release.
- Alerting & gating: wire delta-risk into canary dashboards, a short-lived automatic rollback for red-risk, and human escalation for amber. Integrate Slack alert with a one-click rollback link to the deployment job.
- Observability: attach config SHA and diff metadata to request traces. Export per-config histograms into Console and generate an automated summary report (HTML + JSON) delivered to PRs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run a full matrix (approx 32 configs) on replay+synthetic set within a day on CI infra.
- Delta-risk scores correlate with manual human-labeled regressions on a holdout set (target AUC > 0.85 for detecting >5% functional regression).
- Canary dashboard displays per-slice LQ and latency frontiers and raises the appropriate alert for a staged simulated regression.
- Runbook + rollback link implemented and exercised in a dry-run.

Trade-offs & decisions so far:
- We bias the risk function toward quality over latency because customer-facing correctness failures are higher cost than modest tail increases. This increases false positives for small latency-sensitive micro-optimizations; we will add an override for proven low-impact configs.
- Using embedding similarity as the primary automated quality signal is noisy for open-ended generation; to mitigate we prioritize structured checks for slices where they matter and maintain a human review sample for any amber/red detection.

Next steps (implementation plan):
1) Finalize synthetic prompt set and privacy-safe production sample (Aisha) - DONE (2026-02-25).
2) Implement harness runner that accepts config-delta matrix and emits standardized JSON artifacts (Marco) - in PR.
3) Add tracing metadata instrumentation to runtime (infra) so requests carry config SHA and batch-shape tags (depend on ENG-412345).
4) Build delta-risk calculator and a lightweight UI widget for console canary dashboard (Design + PM).
5) Auto-alert integration with rollback job and runbook.
